podcast.title: The Rosary Murders (1987) – Uncredited Child Actor Appearance as Altar Boy
podcast.body: While serving as an altar boy at the Church of the Holy Redeemer in Detroit, the young Jack Gillis (later Jack White) made an uncredited extra appearance in the 1987 film *The Rosary Murders*. He is visible in the film if you know where to look. This early exposure to acting contributed to his later interest in it as an adult, including a role in *Cold Mountain*. "Technically, this makes Jack White a child actor."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-2000 Superstar Status
podcast.body: Jack White is recognized as one of the few acts to emerge since 2000 who is consistently capable of filling arenas or amphitheaters and achieving substantial success with both streaming and physical media distribution. "Jack White, one of the few acts to emerge since 2000, who was capable of reliably being able to fill an arena or amphitheater and to have substantial success distributing a song through streaming and physical media."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 1: Rock Struggles Again

podcast.title: Founding of Third Man Records (2001)
podcast.body: Jack White established his independent venture, Third Man Records, in Nashville in 2001. The original idea was to release early White Stripes 45s, but it expanded to become a vehicle for his own material and dozens of other indie artists. "He's got his own independent venture, Third Man Records, which is based out of Nashville. Third Man's history goes back to 2001, when Jack and Meg still had the white stripes going into Detroit. The original idea was to release some early white stripes, 45s, but then it just kind of grew from there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Amazon Canoe Wedding (2005) – Karen Elson, Shaman Priest, Three Mystical Rivers
podcast.body: When Jack White married British model Karen Elson in 2005, the ceremony was not held in a Catholic church as one might expect given his devout upbringing. Instead, they were married by a shaman priest in the Amazon basin, at the confluence of three mystical rivers in Brazil, in a canoe. A post-ceremony blessing was administered by a Catholic priest at a nearby church. "They were married by a shaman priest in the Amazon basin at the confluence of three mystical rivers in Brazil."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Multitasking During "Another Way to Die" Video (2008)
podcast.body: The music video for "Another Way to Die," Jack White's collaboration with Alicia Keys for "Quantum of Solace," was filmed in Toronto. This occurred while White was simultaneously promoting his guitar documentary, "It Might Get Loud," demonstrating his busy schedule during the song's release. "The video was shot in Toronto while Jack was promoting his guitar documentary. It might get loud."

podcast.body: Jack White's Third Man Records issued a special 7-inch single for Record Store Day in 2009, featuring his band Dead Weather and the song "Hang You from the Heavens." "Here is a special record store day released from 2009."

podcast.title: 2014 Tour Rider – "No Banana Tour" Policy
podcast.body: Jack White's 2014 tour rider famously included a "no banana tour" policy, explicitly stating, "Seriously, we don't want to see bananas anywhere in the building." The reasons for this strict prohibition were not specified, leading to speculation that it might have been another type of promoter test. "Seriously, we don't want to see bananas anywhere in the building."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 2014 Tour Rider – Exact Guacamole Recipe
podcast.body: Jack White's main requirement in his rider was for fresh guacamole, which had to be made using a very exacting recipe. The rider listed all the necessary ingredients and precisely detailed the methods for combining them, emphasizing that the avocados should "not be mushed too much because we want it chunky." "All the ingredients are listed in the writer, the methods for which they should be combined are listed right there as well. And the avocados must not be mushed too much because we want it chunky."

podcast.title: 21st Century Rock Success
podcast.body: Jack White was listed as a prominent artist from the first decade of the 21st century who could potentially measure up to the alt-rock giants of previous decades, in a discussion about the scarcity of new rock superstars. "Now think about it, outside of Coldplay, Jack White, Gorillas and maybe Lincoln Park. Who else from the first decade of the 21st century can rank against the alt rock giants of the 80s and 90s?"

podcast.title: Advocate for Analog Recording
podcast.body: Jack White's Third Man Records stores in Nashville and Detroit offer a vinyl version of The White Stripes' "Elephant" album that is believed to be fully AAA (Analog recording, Analog mixing, Analog mastering), reflecting his commitment to analog production methods. "If you go to Jack's third man record store in Nashville or Detroit, you can buy a vial version of the elephant album that I'm pretty sure is old school AAA."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Apprenticeship and Punk Rock Exposure
podcast.body: At age 15, Jack White (then Jack Gillis) became an apprentice to Brian Moldun, an upholsterer who exposed him to a wide range of punk rock music, significantly broadening his musical scope. This mentorship led to their musical collaboration as The Upholsterers. "When he was 15, Jack became an apprentice to a guy named Brian Moldun, who ran a place that re-apholstered furniture. While they were working, he exposed Jack to all kinds of punk rock, greatly expanding Jack's musical horizons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Brother and Sister Myth
podcast.body: A persistent myth claimed that Jack and Meg White were brother and sister, which is entirely false. Jack Gillis (his birth name) was the tenth of ten children from a Catholic family in Detroit, with no sister named Meg, while Meg White was from Gross Point Farms with one sister, Heather, and no brothers. This false narrative was deliberately cultivated by Jack White in early interviews, where he referred to Meg as his "little sister," even after their marriage certificate was posted online in 2001. "When you see a band that's two pieces, husband and wife, boyfriend and girlfriend, you think, oh, I see. When their brother and sister, you go, oh, that's interesting. You care more about the music, not the relationship, whether they're trying to save their relationship by being in a band together."

podcast.title: Embracing Cheap Instruments
podcast.body: Jack White is noted for using inexpensive instruments as a deliberate part of his anti-establishment artistic image. This approach contrasts with the use of vintage, high-end guitars and connects him to the indie revival trend of using accessible gear. "They wouldn't be caught dead playing, let's say a vintage-less paw, think white stripes, yeah, yeah, yeah, and the strokes and the black keys."

podcast.title: Favorite Red Airline Rezo Glass Guitar
podcast.body: Jack White's cherished red Airline guitar, specifically the Rezo Glass model, remains one of his absolute favorites. This guitar, built by Velco in 1964 from fiberglass (a cutting-edge material at the time), featured non-traditional body shapes and a short neck with only 20 frets. It was originally sold for $99 at Montgomery Ward department stores but now fetches around $3,000 as a vintage item, and it is featured on every White Stripes album. "One of his absolute favorite guitars remains his red airline. The name of the model is the Rezo Glass."

podcast.title: Hidden Singles
podcast.body: As part of an interesting twist for The Upholsterers project, Jack White and Brian Moldun hid approximately 100 vinyl copies of a 3-track 7-inch single, "Your Furniture was always dead, I was just afraid to tell you," inside couches and chairs they were reupholstering. As of the transcript, only two of these extremely rare copies have been found. "Jack and Brian hid some singles inside couches and chairs that they were fixing up."

podcast.title: Preference for Analog Recording
podcast.body: Jack White is known for his preference for "the old fashioned way" of recording music. This involves using "real to real tape, analog recording consoles," and requiring "take after take after take until they nail their parts," a method that also embraces imperfections for their artistic beauty. "You don't have to be as good as some of the people from the old analog days when you couldn't fix glaring mistakes with digital trickery."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Priesthood Calling Abandoned for Guitar Amplifier – Jack White's Near-Seminary Life
podcast.body: Jack White (born John Anthony Gillis) is the youngest of ten children of Gorman and Theresa Gillis, a devout Catholic couple in Detroit. Both parents worked for the Catholic Archdiocese of Detroit — his mother as a secretary, his father in maintenance. Jack served as an altar boy at the Church of the Holy Redeemer and, following in the footsteps of his six brothers, developed a sense of religious calling. He applied to and was accepted at a seminary in Wisconsin, but had a last-second change of heart when he realized he would not be permitted to bring his new guitar amplifier. He enrolled in public school instead. Had he gone, there would have been no White Stripes, no marriage and divorce to Meg White, and no subsequent marriage to model Karen Elson. "So talk about a decision that changes your life, huh?"

xref.title: First Recording at Sun Studios (1953)
xref.body: On July 18, 1953, a young truck driver named Elvis Presley recorded two songs, "That's When Your Heartaches Begin" and "My Happiness," at Sun Studios in Memphis as a birthday present for his mother. These were Elvis Presley's first recordings ever, and based on this session, studio head Sam Phillips helped Elvis become the iconic figure he would be. This record is argued to be the genesis of all rock and roll. Jack White later purchased this one-of-a-kind artifact for $305,000 US, subsequently digitizing and re-releasing it through Third Man Records so the world could hear it. "This is on July 18th, 1953, a young truck driver dropped into Sun Studios in Memphis to record himself singing a song for his mother."

xref.title: Magic Stick Assault (December 13, 2003) – Jack White Beat Von Bondies Singer Jason Stollsteimer
xref.body: On a Saturday night at the Magic Stick club in Detroit during the CD release party for a local band called Blanche, Jack White approached Von Bondies singer Jason Stollsteimer, spat in his face, and began punching him. When Stollsteimer fell to the floor, White continued hitting him until bystanders pulled him away. White filed a counter-complaint claiming self-defense. He initially pleaded not guilty, then changed his plea to guilty of misdemeanor assault and battery on March 9, 2004. Sentence: $500 fine, $200 court costs, one year of anger management. White maintained that Stollsteimer had grabbed him and pulled out his hair, and that his retaliation lasted less than 10 seconds. He also alleged that Stollsteimer refused to wash off the blood before posing for press photos sent to NME the next morning, and that the permanently damaged eye he claimed was a pre-existing injury from a contact lens incident as a teenager. White and Stollsteimer had not spoken for two years prior to the incident. "The entire event was completely exploited by him, his band and his managers and legal professionals."

xref.title: Breakup in 2011
xref.body: The White Stripes officially announced their breakup on February 2, 2011, stating it was for "a myriad of reasons, mostly to preserve what is beautiful and special about the band." The band had an influential run from 1997 through 2011, becoming a major part of the Indy Rock revival of the early 2000s alongside bands like The Strokes and Arctic Monkeys. The reasons for the split included Meg White's introverted nature and desire for a personal life, the end of her marriage to Jack White, and Jack's diverging musical ambitions. Following the breakup, Meg White receded into obscurity, while Jack White continued as a solo performer and music industry figure. "The official breakup announcement came on February 2, 2011."

xref.title: Altercation with Patrick Carney of The Black Keys
xref.body: On September 13, 2015, Jack White ran into Patrick Carney of The Black Keys at a New York City bar called Cabin Down Below. Carney, who had never met White in person, claimed White tried to fight him, calling White a "40-year-old bully" and saying he inspired Carney to play music as a reaction against such "A-holes." White responded on Twitter, denying any physical altercation, stating he merely asked a question that Carney couldn't answer, and urged him to "speak face to face like a human being." "Patrick, I've never met Jack White until last night. He came to a bar in New York City, I go to a lot with a few friends and tried to fight me."

xref.title: Assault on Jason Stollsteimer of The Von Bondies
xref.body: In December 2003, Jack White was involved in an altercation with Jason Stollsteimer of The Von Bondies at The Magic Stick club in Detroit during a record release party. Reportedly, after being brushed off by Stollsteimer, White allegedly pinned him against speaker stacks, yelled at him, and when Stollsteimer didn't respond, allegedly threw him to the ground, punched him seven times in the face, and spat on him. It took several people to pull White away. This was particularly "weird" as Jack White had previously helped The Von Bondies by producing an album for them and inviting them to open for The White Stripes. "The story is that Jack tried to speak with Jason but was brushed off. Some say Jack pin Jason against the speaker stacks and started yelling."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Attention to Detail and Unified Image
xref.body: The White Stripes, particularly Jack White, are noted for their meticulous attention to every detail of their sound and image, including special uniforms for their roadies. This dedication results in a unified, interesting, and multi-layered aesthetic that contributes to their distinctive identity. "You can tell how much time Jack White spends on every little detail when it comes to the striped sound and image, even their roadies of special uniforms, and the result is something unified, interesting, multi-layered and very cool."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Franz Ferdinand: In Their Own Words

xref.title: Ban from Third Man Studios
xref.body: As part of his feud with The Black Keys, Jack White banned Dan Auerbach from ever setting foot in his Third Man Studios in Nashville. "Hourback was banned from ever-setting foot in Jack's third-man studios in Nashville."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Brother and Sister Myth
xref.body: The idea that Jack and Meg White were brother and sister started as a joke they perpetuated when The White Stripes first began. When they became famous, the truth about their ex-husband and wife relationship was "outed," but some fans continued to believe the original story. "Actually as a joke, when the white stripes started both Jack and Meg insisted that they were brother and sister. But when they got famous, the truth was outed, yet some people refused to believe it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Brother and Sister Myth
xref.body: A persistent myth claimed that Jack and Meg White were brother and sister, which is entirely false. Jack Gillis (his birth name) was the tenth of ten children from a Catholic family in Detroit, with no sister named Meg, while Meg White was from Gross Point Farms with one sister, Heather, and no brothers. This false narrative was deliberately cultivated by Jack White in early interviews, where he referred to Meg as his "little sister," even after their marriage certificate was posted online in 2001. "When you see a band that's two pieces, husband and wife, boyfriend and girlfriend, you think, oh, I see. When their brother and sister, you go, oh, that's interesting. You care more about the music, not the relationship, whether they're trying to save their relationship by being in a band together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Conditional Apology to The Black Keys
xref.body: In the spring of 2014, an apology appeared on Jack White's website, stating, "I wish the Black Keys all the success that they can get." He acknowledged the difficulty of gaining attention for a two-piece band, implying a conditional truce. "I wish the Black Keys all the success that they can get, he said. Lord knows that I can tell you myself how hard it is to get people to pay attention to a two-piece band with a plastic guitar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: In 2013, Jack White made public criticisms against Karen Elson, another of his ex-wives. "And that was followed by shots against Karen Elson, another ex-wife that came in 2013."

xref.title: Extensive Musician Dating History
xref.body: Winona Ryder, an actress, has been connected to or dated a significant number of musicians, totaling 22 individuals according to a count from the transcript. Her relationships included Dave Grohl, Ryan Adams, Pete Yorn, Jack White, Julian from The Strokes, Conor Oberst of Bright Eyes, possibly Jeff Tweedy from Wilco, Irish musician Damien Rice, Tre Cool of Green Day, Marky Walberg (Marky Mark), Stephen Jenkins of Third Eye Blind, Everlast (whose real name is Eric Shorty), John Kay from Jamiroquai, Adam Duritz of Counting Crows (who also dated Jennifer Aniston and Courtney Cox), Chris Isaak, Dave Pirner of Soul Asylum, Paul Westerberg of The Replacements (which was noted as potentially during her "Minneapolis punk period"), Mike Nesmith of The Monkees, Johnny Depp, and Evan Dando of The Lemonheads. The last heard connection was an engagement to Blake Sennett, who plays guitar in Rilo Kiley. "I count 22 musicians."

xref.title: Female Elvis Presley
xref.body: Wanda Jackson was known by the moniker "the female Elvis Presley" and is a significant figure in rock and roll history, with musician Jack White expressing admiration for her work. "There was one to Jackson, otherwise known as the female Elvis Presley. Jack White is a big fan of her."

xref.body: In 2006, Jack White had a beef with English indie guitarist Billy Childish. "a beef with English Indie guitarist Billy Childish in 2006."

xref.title: Feud with Filmmaker over Footage
xref.body: In 2004, Jack White had a dispute with a filmmaker concerning unauthorized performance footage of The White Stripes. "Moving on to more Jack White feuds, there was a fight with a filmmaker in 2004 about some unauthorized white stripes performance footage."

xref.title: Feud with Jack White
xref.body: Jack White harbored disdain for The Black Keys, particularly guitarist Dan Auerbach, whom he called a "copycat." The animosity escalated when White accused Auerbach of interfering in his custody dispute with ex-wife Karen Elson, specifically over their children attending the same Nashville private school as Auerbach's children from another relationship. Leaked emails from 2013 contained "vicious" remarks. "For some reason, Jack had a disdain for guitarist Dan Hourback, calling him a copycat and calling him out for allegedly getting involved in the custody battle he was having with Karen Elson, that ex-wife."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Feud with Ryan Adams over Song Covers
xref.body: In 2002, Jack White publicly attacked Ryan Adams in the press for covering several White Stripes songs and changing some of their lyrics. The dispute continued for a while before Adams offered positive remarks about The White Stripes, and the conflict faded. "2002, Ryan Adams covers several white striped songs but changed some of the lyrics. Jack attacked Adams and depressed for this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Feud with The Black Keys
xref.body: Jack White expressed disdain for The Black Keys' guitarist Dan Auerbach, calling him a "copycat." The feud intensified when White accused Auerbach of allegedly involving himself in White's custody battle with ex-wife Karen Elson, specifically noting that Auerbach sent his children to the same Nashville private school as White's and Elson's children. Leaked emails from 2013 between White and Elson revealed vicious comments. "For some reason, Jack had a disdain for guitarist Dan Hourback, calling him a copycat and calling him out for allegedly getting involved in the custody battle he was having with Karen Elson, that ex-wife."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation and Persona
xref.body: Jack White, a former altar boy and furniture upholsterer, and Meg White, a shy, non-musical bartender, met, fell in love, married, and began jamming together. They cultivated a public persona of being brother and sister while releasing stripped-down bluesy garage rock music on indie labels. "A former altar boy and furniture a poster and the youngest child and a Detroit family of ten meets a shy, non-musical bartender. They fall in love, they get married, they start jamming together, pretend that their brother and sister and start releasing stripped down bluesy garage rock music on a series of indie labels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hidden Singles Initiative
xref.body: Brian Moldun collaborated with Jack White in hiding about 100 vinyl copies of their 3-track 7-inch single, "Your Furniture was always dead, I was just afraid to tell you," within furniture they had reupholstered. "Jack and Brian hid some singles inside couches and chairs that they were fixing up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Industry Recognition and Collaborations
xref.body: Their talent garnered attention from prominent musicians; Jack White was such a fan that The White Stripes recorded one of their songs. They also developed friendships with members of Death Cab for Cutie and embarked on tours with acclaimed artists such as Neil Young, Weezer, The Black Keys, Cake, Bryan Adams, and Sious and Colour. "Jack White was such a fan that the white stripes recorded one of their songs. They became friends with members of Death Cab for Cutie."

xref.body: Following the incident, Jack White pleaded guilty to aggravated assault, was fined $750, and ordered to attend an anger management course. "In the end, Jack pleaded guilty to aggravated assault. He was fined $750 and told to take an anger management course."

xref.title: Marriage and Divorce
xref.body: Jack and Meg White were married on September 21, 1996, with Jack Gillis adopting Meg's last name to become Jack White. They divorced in March 2000 but continued to be bandmates and friends, even attending and serving in each other's subsequent wedding parties. "The truth is that Jack and Meg were married on September 21, 1996, but then divorced in March of 2000."

xref.title: Meg White's Lead Vocal Contributions
xref.body: Despite Jack White performing the vast majority of lead vocals, Meg White sang lead on five tracks for The White Stripes, in addition to providing backup vocals on several others. "Meg White saying on several tracks as backup and as lead on five tracks"

xref.body: Fall Out Boy was among the artists, including Blink-182, Green Day, Coldplay, Jack White, Red Hot Chili Peppers, Slipknot, Queens of the Stone Age, Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters, U2, Linkin Park, Evanescence, and David Bowie, who achieved number one records during the 2010s. This demonstrated the continued success of rock acts in an era where hip hop was a dominant cultural force. "Link wanted a two Green Day Coldplay Jack White, Red Hotch-Lie Pepper, Slipp-Nont, Queens of the Stone Age, Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters, U2, Link and Park Follow Boy, Evan Essence, Queens of the Stone Age, and Bowie all had number one records over the course of the decade."

xref.title: Post-Breakup Lives
xref.body: After the band's dissolution, Meg White reportedly lives quietly in Detroit, while Jack White divides his time between Nashville and Detroit. They maintain infrequent contact. "As far as anyone could tell, Meg lives quietly in Detroit, and Jack spends most of his time in Nashville, although he goes back and forth to Detroit. They'll talk, but not that often."

xref.body: Jack White made "ill-advised remarks" to a group of vegans in a Brooklyn park in 2010. In 2012, he made public criticisms against Lady Gaga, Twitter, Clint Eastwood, and even his ex-wife Meg White. "Some ill-advised remarks to a group of vegans in a Brooklyn park in 2010, shots against Lady Gaga against Twitter against Clint Eastwood and even ex-wife Meg White in 2012."

xref.body: Following a public Twitter exchange, Patrick Carney announced that he had spoken with Jack White for an hour, finding him "cool, all good." He's cool, all good. Jack responded from one musician to another. You have my respect, Patrick Carney."

xref.title: Riff Origin Anecdote
xref.body: Jack White spontaneously created the signature seven-note riff for "Seven Nation Army" during a soundcheck on January 29, 2002, at the Corner Hotel in Melbourne, Australia. He found the riff "cool" and played it repeatedly, even though Ben Swank from Third Man Records initially disliked it and suggested Jack "can do better." White even considered it for a James Bond theme before deciding to use it for a White Stripes song. "Jack White came up with a seven note riff, which he thought sounded cool, so he played it over and over and over again."

xref.title: Signature Guitar's Widespread and Unorthodox Appeal
xref.body: The Ernie Ball Music Man St. Vincent Signature Model, with its "retro, future" and "unorthodox shape," has garnered appeal across diverse genres. It has been played by notable artists like Jack White (on SNL) and Tom Morello, and even metalheads (via a stealth black version) and country players, highlighting its versatility and unique design. "Jack White played it on SNL. Tom Morello has one. I've seen, we make an all black version. It's like the stealth version, which is for metalheads. And metal dudes play it. There's country players who are playing it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: UK Success and Jack White Co-Production
xref.body: Like The White Stripes and The Strokes, The Von Bondis initially found significant attention in the UK. They toured with The White Stripes and other young Garage Rock bands, and Jack White notably co-produced their first album, "Lack of Communication." "It just like the Stripes in the Strokes, the first territory to pay close attention was the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Upholstery Background and Taxidermy Hobby
xref.body: Before breaking into the music business, Jack White was an apprentice upholsterer. He even formed a band with his boss called "The Upholsterers," and they recorded an album. More recently, Jack has taken up taxidermy. "In fact, he wasn't apprentice of poster her before he broke into the music business."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Upholstery Shop Mentor
xref.body: Brian Moldun ran an upholstery shop where Jack White (then Jack Gillis) apprenticed at age 15, introducing him to punk rock. Moldun convinced Jack to make a record together, playing drums himself while Jack played guitar. "When he was 15, Jack became an apprentice to a guy named Brian Moldun, who ran a place that re-apholstered furniture."
